capabilities: Store structured records in plain-text .duowei JSON files inside the vault
Edit tables with 22 field types, formula fields, relations, lookup, and rollup
Display data as grid, kanban, gallery, calendar, timeline, form, or dashboard views
Import and export CSV/TSV and convert from Bases files or vault folders
Bind records to Markdown notes, sync fields with frontmatter, and embed views in notes
disambiguation: Not a Markdown table editor; records live in standalone .duowei JSON files, with Markdown binding and frontmatter sync as optional extras.
extras: The plugin interface, commands, and settings are in Simplified Chinese only; the English README is a translation. A separately distributed Pro edition adds AI fields and external calendar/task sync and must not be enabled alongside the Community Edition.
problem: Obsidian has no local, plain-text record database that keeps rows independent of Markdown files while offering multiple views, formulas, and relations over the data.
summary: Spreadsheet-style structured data stored in plain-text .duowei JSON files, with 22 field types, seven view types, formulas, relations, and CSV/TSV import/export.
